reading.body:
Gabe Amo's AI record is eleven PAC contributions from five large technology companies and four votes or cosponsorships on AI and semiconductor bills, with no event in the data showing a contribution and a vote on the same bill.

The money is consistent and modest. Amazon's PAC gave four times between May 2025 and June 2026, totaling $8,500. Google's NETPAC gave three times, $4,000. Meta's PAC gave twice, $6,000. Microsoft's and Oracle's PACs each gave once, $2,500 and $1,000. Every contribution is dated before the June 2026 vote on H.R. 7757, but the data does not say what that bill does or whether any donor had an interest in it.

The legislative side is thin on detail. Four items are recorded: cosponsorship of the AI-WISE Act, the RESTRICT Act, and the LIFT AI Act, plus yea votes on three bills identified only by number. The descriptions give bill titles for the cosponsorships and nothing for the votes. Nothing here establishes that any contribution influenced any vote, and the page states it draws no conclusion about motives.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no record of committee assignments, no text of the bills, no indication of whether the AI-WISE, RESTRICT, or LIFT AI Acts touch compute, data centers, or power. A reader cannot tell from this whether Amo's AI legislation addresses the grid constraint or only enterprise adoption and export controls. The record shows a member taking money from AI firms and voting on AI bills. It does not show the two connecting.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Gabe Amo: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 19 events.
